title: Parliamentary Expenses Amendment (Transparency and Accountability) Bill 2015
short_title: Parliamentary Expenses Amendment (Transparency and Accountability) Bill 2015

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would require public disclosure of parliamentary travel benefit claims, introduce penalties for excess claims and extend Commonwealth Ombudsman oversight to entitlement claims.
Claimants would lodge monthly explanations with the Department of Finance within seven days after month end, and the department would publish them within 14 days of receipt.
Ordinary disclosure would exclude travel for parliamentary sittings and committee business, with national security grounds allowing relevant travel purposes to be listed as confidential.
changes: Charter travel statements would have to explain why charter transport was necessary or desirable compared with commercial services.
Family travel statements would identify the relationship of each traveller and provide travel details and total costs.
Excess travel claims paid by the Commonwealth could attract financial loadings unless attributable to departmental administrative error.
The Ombudsman could investigate entitlement claims and provide assessments for ministerial consideration and parliamentary reporting.
summary.affected: Parliamentarians, parliamentary office-holders, ministers, their travelling families, the Department of Finance and the Commonwealth Ombudsman would be affected.
